research_question: Can a source-observed merge event and a current ruleset whose creation/update timestamps precede merge certify the fully effective historical policy and legitimate edit authority?

comparison.strong_classical: Open-world temporally indexed layered policy model: current minimum 0 approvals plus conditionally extra approval does not certify 2026-09-30 state, effective protections/bypass or normative rights
comparison.weak_baseline: treat current required review count 0 and successful merge as permission for every edit (unsound)
comparison.preregistered_after_discovery: This packet is a disclosure and replay lock made AFTER discovery; no novel unsighted prediction claim.

research_limits: Current rule state is not retroactively an independently verified versioned policy snapshot
Ruleset updated_at is a provider metadata claim; even if before event, it does not enumerate historic classic branch protections and org bypass actors
COMMENTED review events are not APPROVED events
A platform successful merge event is not a demonstration of normative legitimate authority
Do not change upstream source or branch policies
No new architecture law can be authorized from this governance replay
Zero unconditional required approving reviews does not mean no conditional extra approval; require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes is true in current ruleset
current_user_can_bypass=never is a present requesting-account property, not a historical predicate on merge actor vishr
bypass_actors key absent from public rule response must NOT be interpreted as no bypass actors
